analysis.description: The two opening canonic subject statements only; the bass is accompaniment. This movement has no fugal exposition, and its later material is not represented.

notes: Foster identifies this movement as an accompanied two-voice canon and explicitly states that the bass does not give the subject. Accordingly, only the two opening canonic statements are plotted; the bass accompaniment lane is empty. This is an opening canon excerpt, not a complete fugue exposition. The recurring countersubject and the new subject in the second half are outside this map. Manual score transcription of opening subject and answer statements, checked against Dorothy Nell Foster (1973), Chapter IV. Quarter-note units; entry ends include the final note and all its written ties. Excerpts extend through the final subject release when it passes the exposition cadence. No recording timing has been estimated. A short independently engraved subject incipit is included; the source score, thesis prose and chart images are not redistributed.
